rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Rutherford fired α-particles at thin gold foil: most passed undeflected (the atom is mostly empty space), but ~1 in 8000 suffered large-angle deflections — impossible unless a tiny, massive, positive **nucleus** concentrated the charge and mass. The nucleus (R ~ 10⁻¹⁵ m, vs atom 10⁻¹⁰ m) holds Z protons and N = A − Z neutrons, bound by the short-range strong nuclear force.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - R = R₀A^(1/3), R₀ ≈ 1.2 fm - ρ_nucleus ≈ 2×10¹⁷ kg/m³ - N = A − Z

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Alpha Particle Source: Rutherford used alpha particles (helium nuclei, +2e charge, ~5 MeV energy) from radioactive decay (radium/polonium).  ·  Thin Foil: Gold foil used because gold is highly malleable — can be made extremely thin (~400 atoms thick) so alpha particles interact with at most one atom.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Nearly all the mass and all the positive charge of an atom are concentrated in a tiny central nucleus."

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Nucleus vs atom size:** 10⁻¹⁵ m vs 10⁻¹⁰ m — the nucleus is 100,000× smaller but holds ~all the mass.  ·  **Electrons cannot deflect α-particles** — they are ~7300× lighter.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Finding the Needle in the Atom Thomson's "plum pudding" atom filled space with positive charge. Rutherford's gold-foil experiment blew it apart: nearly all the mass and all the positive charge sit in a tiny, dense **nucleus** — an object 10⁻¹⁵ m across holding 99.9% of the atom's mass.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Rutherford's scattering experiment (1911) α-particles (helium nuclei) were fired at a thin gold foil (~10⁻⁷ m, a few hundred atoms thick): - **Most passed straight through** — the atom is mostly empty space. - **A few deflected by large angles (>90°)** — some encountered a small, massive, positively charged core.…

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): Show nuclear density is independent of A.** — Mass ∝ A, volume ∝ R³ ∝ A (since R ∝ A^(1/3)), so ρ = mass/volume is constant ≈ 2×10¹⁷ kg/m³.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Present the experiment as observation → inference, point by point.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Large-angle α scattering proved the nucleus** — like a cannonball bouncing off tissue paper.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Rutherford: mostly empty atom; tiny dense positive nucleus; Z protons, N = A − Z neutrons.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Nuclear density ~2×10¹⁷ kg/m³ is nearly the same for every nucleus from helium to uranium.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### Deep dive: what the scattering angles really said Rutherford's team fired alpha particles at gold foil and watched the angles. Most alphas sailed straight through — the atom is mostly empty. rows.text: Point Charge Approximation: Alpha particle treated as point charge; nucleus treated as point charge — valid since distances are much larger than nuclear/alpha sizes.  ·  No verified PYQ; NEB-style practice (Rutherford description 3–4m, density 3m).  ·  Why did Rutherford use gold foil?
